'''Gokana''' ('''Gòkánà''') is an [[Ogoni languages|Ogoni language]] spoken by some 130,000 people in [[Rivers State]], [[Nigeria]].

==Phonology==
Gokana has been argued to lack [[syllables]], a radical claim because syllables are traditionally considered to be [[Language universal|universal]]. According to Hyman (1983), Gokana "does not organise its consonants and vowels into syllables." Hyman later amended his claim to say that "the syllable plays at best a minor role in the [[Prosody (linguistics)|prosodic]] organisation of Gokana" and is perhaps not activated to express any generalisations in the language.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hyman |first1=Larry |title=Does Gokana really have no syllables? Or: what's so great about being universal? |journal=Phonology |date=May 2011 |volume=28 |issue=1 |pages=55–57|doi=10.1017/S0952675711000030 |s2cid=31005113 |url=http://www.escholarship.org/uc/item/9b48r86x }}</ref>

[[Nasal vowels]] are indicated by a tilde and [[Tone (linguistics)|tones]] are indicated by an acute or grave accent:
* The high tone is indicated by an acute accent : á, ã́, é, ẹ́, ẽ́, í, ĩ́, ó, ọ́, ṍ, ú, ṹ, ḿ;
* The low tone is indicated by a grave accent  : à, ã̀, è, ẹ̀, ẽ̀, ì, ĩ̀, ò, ọ̀, õ̀, ù, ũ̀, m̀;
* The middle tone is indicated with no diacritic.
